title: The B58 identity certificate: commit P of build step 2 against cf43fbb
what: Commit P of build step 2 (ORDER step 14; the interface sheet 6; rows 94, 117, 127, 136, 138-140 and 146) makes the preview horizon H a parameter of the environment, takes fingerprint schema 4 (transmission, the training and scoring backends with their contract, the protocol, preview_h_s and reward_knock among the FATAL fields), reads engines.trainable() from the committed records, and gives the reward its knock option. It edits two files of PLANT_CODE, engine_env.py and engines.py, so the B58's plant_sha moves; nothing it changes is meant to move a number the B58 computes at its defaults (row 94). Before P lands on GRA-test, the B58 built through it has to be X1's plant, the plant of cf43fbb: the same doubles, not the same figures to a tolerance. This page says how that was measured and what came out. results/B58_IDENTITY.json holds every number below, read by make_cert.py from the run groups' records and the runs' own output files; the tools, the plans of the run and the evidence are archived beside it (section 7).

notes.nothing_computed_moved: Every value the harness, L6 and build_dataset compared is meant to be the same double in both trees (the counts are in the verdict line), and every writer's output and every report to equal cf43fbb's; the differences section 5 lists are labels, code hashes, run times and committed files older than the code on both trees.
notes.why_plant_sha_moves: plant_sha hashes the code of fingerprint.plant_files('b58') -- plant.py, thermal.py, engine_env.py, derived.py and engines.py -- and the values of the B58's two spec files. P edits engine_env.py (H a parameter, the reward's knock option) and engines.py (trainable() read from the committed records), so plant_sha moves although no computed value is meant to; it names P's plant, which every later step of build step 2 is compared against. fingerprint.py, which P also edits, is not in PLANT_CODE.
notes.why_engine_sha_does_not_move: engine_sha hashes every value of the plant as built (engines.engine_sha), and P adds and changes no field of the B58's records: engine_sha is commit A's (a check of section 1), and over build step 1's key set it is still build step 1's (amendment B11).
notes.fingerprint_fields: Schema 4 (P): plant_sha, plant_text_sha and engine_sha name the code and the record set; transmission holds the gearing (final_drive and gears, which schema 3 printed as fields of their own, read here out of it for the shared fields); train_backend, score_backend and backend_contract replace schema 3's backend; preview_h_s, reward_knock and preview_samples_s are new; git_head names the commit the run was on. The reference, a git archive of cf43fbb, has no git fields and no engine fields (schema 2).
notes.first_run: The first run of this certificate's groups (7-8 November 2026, 16:08Z to 03:00Z, 39139 s beside the roads check) wrote 101 PASS and 5 FAIL records: G1-harness record 29, G3-roads record 2, G5-app-lab record 10, G7-suites records 12 and 16. All five were defects of the kit's driver (tools/cert_driver_P.sh), not of P: in each, the evidence places the fault in the driver's check, not in P's output. In G3.1, G7.2 and G7.4 the output under test met the expectation CERT_PLAN_A.md and CERT_PLAN_P.md state. In G1.7(b) the two JSONs and the two pages were byte-identical, which is what B9 asks, and three of the five makes exited 1, each only when printing, after writing its JSON: the driver ran them without -X utf8, and commit A's make_cert.py and P's alike stopped printing commit A's re-checked FAIL record G5-app-lab 22 (Arabic text) to a cp1252 stdout. In G5.2 the launcher met its expectation ('is ready', exit 124), and --check ran only as its server stopped: the driver waited for a line launch.py prints to block-buffered stdout, which reaches the file only at the launcher's exit. G3.1 asked the --road random run for the default run's last line; G7.2's parser missed RealTree's ok, printed on a line of its own after RealTree's stderr line; G7.4 grepped one line for a rule that wraps (CLAUDE.md:137-138). The driver was corrected (TOOL_EDITS.md, section 'commit P', its part 'commit P, second edit'), reviewed again, installed on the same S after the roads check ended (TOOL_EDITS.md, section 'commit P, second install'), and G1, G3, G5 and G7 re-run there with cert-recheck: the re-check records say what each re-run found. The five FAIL records stay in this certificate; a re-run PASS record that re-checks one names it (rechecks), and the FAIL gains rechecked_by. The edited checks keep the first run's what and command texts, so that every run of one check is the same check: the re-run records of the checks of G1-harness record 29, G5-app-lab record 10 and G7-suites record 16 therefore carry the first run's command text (python -I -B; once it printed 'is ready'; the one-line grep), and each says in its expected what ran (-X utf8 on the five makes; --check once the server had logged the launcher's GET / with status 200; the rule's line and its continuation), as INTEGRATION.md section 7 does.
